summary.summary: Arun ended 2025/26 with £35.46m of PWLB debt — four maturity loans taken in 2012 for HRA housing self-financing at an average 3.40%, the first not repayable until 2030 — against a capital financing requirement of £52.06m, leaving £16.6m covered by internal cash instead of loans. No new borrowing was taken during the year, and planned borrowing-funded capital spending largely did not happen (£2.956m unfinanced capital expenditure against an original £27.913m), so the CFR barely moved. Investment income was £2.3m against a £2.02m budget on average balances of about £53m. The council's two CCLA pooled funds are worth £559k less than the £7m put in — a loss parked behind the IFRS 9 statutory override until March 2029, with a £500k equalisation reserve set aside against it.

signals.headline: Verified quiet: no new borrowing in 2025/26; £35.46m HRA PWLB debt (first maturity 28/3/2030) against £52.06m CFR; investment income £275k over budget
signals.why: An under-borrowed district with a fixed, distant-maturity debt book and returns beating budget presents no near-term treasury concern.

news_drafts.headline: Arun's housing stock survey rated Red, blocking compliance reporting and investment planning
news_drafts.lead: Arun's survey of its 3,430-home stock has been rated Red—the lowest assessment—by an external consultant, preventing the council from reliably reporting Decent Homes compliance or planning major investment. The survey, designed in-house with non-standard scoring and no quality assurance, shows 41.90% of homes decent and 43.37% non-decent, but the consultant states this figure will likely overestimate actual compliance because survey data is incomplete and methodology is non-compliant with Decent Homes standards. The assessment blocks calculation of service charges for 473 leaseholder properties and prevents the council capturing communal maintenance costs needed for a full 30-year housing investment plan. The council faces immediate pressure: its Warm Homes Wave 3 programme is already running at £16,463 per property against a £7,500 grant assumption, and 424 properties needing upgrade to meet the 2030 EPC C energy efficiency requirement lie outside current funding programmes.

news_drafts.headline: Arun's housing survey data rated red; council unable to assess stock condition or plan investment
news_drafts.lead: Arun Council cannot reliably assess the condition of its 3,430 homes or plan maintenance investment because its stock condition survey is methodologically flawed and lacks quality assurance, according to an external consultant's report to the Housing and Wellbeing Committee on 24 September. The survey, designed in-house with non-standard scoring and conducted by three different companies with inconsistent results, has been rated red by the consultant. Of 3,430 units, 681 properties and 103 blocks remain unsurveyed. The report warns that current reporting of Decent Homes compliance — the statutory standard for safe, warm and modern housing — significantly under-reports the actual position because criteria assessments are incomplete. Investment planning is incomplete because the survey excludes communal elements, balconies and other components for which the council is financially responsible. The consultant states the council cannot calculate service charge liabilities for 473 leaseholder properties in blocks or assess funding adequacy without complete data. The council has also identified that the Warm Homes Wave 3 energy-efficiency programme is running at £8,963 per property above grant allowance, leaving a gap for the 424 properties not yet covered.

news_drafts.headline: Arun housing stock survey rated RED, cannot reliably support planning
news_drafts.lead: The council's housing stock survey has been rated RED for quality and cannot reliably support planning decisions. The survey of the housing revenue account stock—the account through which council-owned housing is financed from rents—has yet to assess 681 units. It lacks written guidance to assessors, shows inconsistencies across three contractors, and has no quality assurance. Reported compliance with the government's Decent Homes standard stands at 41.90%, but the figure is unreliable and likely overstates the council's position. The council cannot calculate maintenance costs for communal areas or service charges for its 473 leaseholder properties in blocks. Meanwhile, costs on the Warm Homes energy programme are running at £16,463 per property against a budgeted £7,500.

findings.headline: Emergency repairs completion rate falls 18 percentage points below target in single quarter
findings.detail: Emergency repair completion within timescale fell to 80.12% this quarter from 98.83% previous quarter, well below 95% target. Manager notes remaining overdue repairs are increasingly complex. Daily monitoring and contractor KPIs are in place to manage.
findings.matters: Sharp performance deterioration may indicate contractor issues or resource constraints; complexity of outstanding repairs suggests potential cost pressures.
findings.figures: 80.12% of 387 emergency repairs completed within timescale (target 95%), down from 98.83% previous quarter

findings.headline: Damp and mould response reports issued within 3-day target fell to 20.34% from 100% last quarter; Category 1 hazard cases rose to 5 from zero
findings.detail: Reports issued within 3-day target dropped from 100% last quarter to 20.34% this quarter. Category 1 hazard cases rose from zero to five; Category 2 cases increased from 86 to 139. Performance data indicates acute operational strain in damp and mould response.
findings.matters: Indicates loss of compliance capability in handling damp and mould; risks tenant health impacts and satisfaction; suggests resource or process failure.
findings.figures: Reports in timescale: 20.34% vs target 100% and previous 100% (6 reports issued); CAT1 cases: 5 open vs 0 previous quarter; CAT2 cases: 139 vs 86
findings.quote: Reports issued within 3 days of inspection completion 100% 20.34% 100% 6

findings.headline: Outstanding fire remedial actions increased 48% to 2,204 against a zero target; waking watch implemented at three Hastings Close blocks
findings.detail: Outstanding FRA remedial actions increased from 1,496 last quarter to 2,204 (target: zero). Council has implemented waking watch at Hastings Close blocks after determining existing fire mitigations were insufficient. Procurement of additional fire remedial contractors is ongoing, indicating contractor capacity constraints.
findings.matters: Signals serious fire safety compliance gap; waking watch is expensive interim measure; contractor capacity issues delay remediation of material fire risk.
findings.figures: 2,204 outstanding remedial actions (target 0), up 48% from 1,496; comprising 35 Very High, 1,643 High, 377 Medium, 149 Low priority items
findings.quote: we have concluded that the current mitigations that are in place in blocks with fire risk remedial actions were not sufficient at the three Hastings Close blocks and as such have implemented a waking watch.

findings.headline: Specialist audit found 43.38% of surveyed housing stock (1,234 properties) does not meet Decent Homes Standard against 100% target
findings.detail: A specialist consultant identified significant errors in previous assessment methodology. Reanalysed stock data shows 1,234 properties (43.38%) do not meet Decent Homes Standard against a 100% target. Investment plans to address this have been prepared and are now with the HRA business plan consultant for fundability assessment.
findings.matters: Reveals material capital requirement for housing remediation; HRA's capacity to fund the program is uncertain, affecting future borrowing plans and service delivery.
findings.figures: 1,529 homes (56.62%) meet standard; 1,234 homes (43.38%) do not; target 100%
findings.quote: The remodel of the stock data using the correct definitions, shows 56.62% of the surveyed stock is decent. This equates to 1,234 surveyed properties not being decent.

findings.headline: Data integrity issues identified as principal risk with further measure revisions expected
findings.detail: Data integrity listed as principal service risk. Compliance team conducting ongoing data validation and assurance on all compliance areas, with note that this may lead to revised measures in Q2. Mirrors Q1 stock condition reassessment that revealed material differences from previous methodology.
findings.matters: Ongoing data validation may reveal further reporting gaps affecting financial and operational position reliability.
findings.figures: Data integrity listed as principal risk; validation work ongoing
findings.quote: The compliance team are working with business improvement to continue to carry out data validation and assurance on all compliance areas, this may lead to revised measures in Q2.
